# Schildersafari

> An open-source, offline-first game for collecting German number-plate area codes and discovering the places behind them.

Schildersafari is available in German and English, selected from browser language with a saved manual override. It covers 716 regional codes, grouped into 13 collections by Bundesland (combining Berlin/Brandenburg, Bremen/Niedersachsen and Hamburg/Schleswig-Holstein).

Players enter an area code, such as B or HH, to mark it seen and unlock its place and a sourced fact. Unseen codes are represented by question marks. Every code has a researched story in German and English, with a source link. Stories cover local curiosities, history, nature and traditions; folklore is explicitly presented as legend.

The PWA works offline after its first complete online load. Sightings are stored locally in IndexedDB, with no account or cloud sync. GPS is entirely optional: a user can save or update their current position for a spotted plate. No location is requested on startup, no background tracking is used, and coordinates stay on the device. Text backups transfer codes and dates, but exclude GPS locations.

## Links
- [App](https://schildersafari.de/): Canonical app URL.
- [Source and documentation](https://github.com/jewell-lgtm/plates): MIT-licensed app code, setup instructions, data provenance and tests.
- [Author](https://mattjewell.co.uk): Matt Jewell.
- [Catalogue source](https://www.adac.de/rund-ums-fahrzeug/auto-kaufen-verkaufen/kfz-zulassung/kfz-kennzeichen-deutschland/): ADAC catalogue dated 14 September 2026. This app uses a snapshot, not a live registry.

## Technical summary
Expo / React Native / TypeScript; service-worker precaching using Workbox. Static HTTPS hosting. Existing browser data from the former plates app can be exported and imported through About. Registrations and vehicle owners are not tracked.
